## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$,
$H_0=-\Delta$, $H_\gamma=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and let
$U_D(t)$ be the Dollard-modified evolution of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-integrable-remainder]], with modified wave operators $\Omega_{D\pm}=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_\gamma}U_D(t)$, whose existence on all of $L^2$ is included in the claimed conclusion. Then:

(a) $\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH_0}=e^{-isH_\gamma}\Omega_{D\pm}$ for all $s$;

(b) *Per-channel form.* With the Coulomb angular-radial unitary
$\widehat T_{\gamma,l}$ and its free analogue $\widehat T_{0,l}$ constructed
below with regular coefficient one and density $\sqrt E/(\pi|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2)$, the operator $\Omega_{D\pm}$ acts in
each angular channel as multiplication by a bounded Borel function $b_{l,\pm}(E)$
of the energy;

(c) *Completeness.* $|b_{l,\pm}(E)|=1$ for a.e. $E>0$, hence
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\gamma)=H_{\mathrm{c}}(H_\gamma)$
and the modified scattering operator $S_D=\Omega_{D+}^*\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$.

The statement covers the exactly Coulombic two-body model with $\gamma>0$; it
does not assert explicit scattering amplitudes or measured cross sections.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\gamma>0$, $H_0=-\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and
$H_\gamma:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(H_\gamma)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, the
self-adjoint Coulomb operator established below on this exact domain, with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$ as proved by the local compact-resolvent argument. Use the physical-momentum Fourier transform $\mathcal F_pf(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\mathcal F_2f(p/(2\pi))$, unitary by the dilation change of variables, equivalently $(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x}f(x)dx$ on Schwartz functions. Let $P_j=\mathcal F_p^*M_{p_j}\mathcal F_p=-i\partial_j$ on its maximal weak-derivative domain; thus $H_0=\mathcal F_p^*M_{|p|^2}\mathcal F_p$. Set $a(p)=\gamma/(2|p|)$ for $p\ne0$ and $a(0)=0$, and $a(P)=\mathcal F_p^*M_a\mathcal F_p$ on the maximal multiplier domain. For $|t|\ge1$ define the
Dollard-modified free evolution
$$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}e^{i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\,a(P)\log|t|}$$
(the two factors commute, being functions of $P$; extend to $|t|\le1$ by
$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}$). Then:

(a) $U_D(t)$ is unitary for every $t$ and strongly continuous in $t$ away from $t=0$; on the dense set of momentum $C_c^\infty$ vectors supported in an annulus $0<a_0\le|p|\le b_0<\infty$ it is differentiable for $|t|>1$, with the exterior one-sided derivatives at $t=\pm1$, and
$$i\,U_D'(t)=\Bigl[H_0-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\qquad(|t|>1).$$

(b) *Integrable remainder.* For every vector $\psi$ in that dense set one has
$$\int_1^\infty\Bigl\|\Bigl[\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\psi\Bigr\|_2dt<\infty,$$
and the same integral with $|t|$ in the comparison denominator over $(-\infty,-1]$ is finite. More precisely, for each such $\psi$ there are $T_\psi\ge1$ and $C_\psi<\infty$ such that for both signs of $t$, $|t|\ge T_\psi$ implies $\|[\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|t|\,|P|)]U_D(t)\psi\|_2\le C_\psi(1+\log|t|)/|t|^2$.

No empirical claim, no Rutherford cross-section and no photon interpretation is
asserted; the logarithmic phase is a comparison construction for the
long-range generator.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with a specified norm-dense sequence $(d_j)_{j\ge1}$, with
inner product linear in the first argument. Let $A$ be a densely defined
self-adjoint operator on $H$. There is a unique regular projection-valued
Borel measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ representing $A$, with $E(\mathbb R)=I$,
strong countable additivity, and the exact domain and norm identity

$$D(A)=\{h:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2d\mu_h(\lambda)<\infty\},\qquad \|Ah\|^2=\int\lambda^2d\mu_h,\qquad \mu_h(B)=\langle E(B)h,h\rangle.$$

Here regular means that every finite positive scalar measure $\mu_h$ is
inner regular by compact sets and outer regular by open sets. Every bounded
Borel function $b$ has a uniquely determined bounded operator $b(A)$, with
$\|b(A)\|\le\sup|b|$, $(bc)(A)=b(A)c(A)$ and
$\overline b(A)=b(A)^*$. Every possibly unbounded complex Borel function
$b$ has a closed densely defined multiplication realization with exact domain
$\{h:\int|b|^2d\mu_h<\infty\}$ when $b$ is finite valued; its truncations
converge on that domain. In particular $e^{itA}$ is a strongly continuous
unitary group and

$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac{e^{itA}h-h}{t}=iAh\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\in D(A).$$

Regular representing PVMs and this calculus transport under unitary
intertwiners. An isometry intertwining the two strongly continuous groups
has a reducing closed range and intertwines their PVMs. These conclusions
use the specified countable dense sequence and CC, with no general
AC spectral theorem, Gelfand representation, Riesz-Markov theorem or Stone
existence theorem as a premise.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$, let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), and let
$(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
$L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]. Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with Lebesgue measure and inner product linear
in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and let
$$K:=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2\bigl((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C\bigr)$$
be the Hilbert direct sum over $l\ge0$, $-l\le m\le l$. For $\psi\in L^2$ and
each $(l,m)$ define the coefficient function and the reduced function
$$c_{lm}(r):=\int_{S^2}\psi(r\Omega)\overline{Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\quad(r>0,\ \text{a.e.}),\qquad u_{lm}(r):=r\,c_{lm}(r).$$
Then:

(a) for every $\psi\in L^2$ and every $(l,m)$ the function $u_{lm}$ is a well-defined element of $L^2((0,\infty),dr)$ depending only on the class of $\psi$, and $U\psi:=(u_{lm})_{l,m}$ is a linear isometry of $L^2$ into (indeed onto) $K$ with
$$\|U\psi\|_K^2=\sum_{l\ge0}\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\int_0^\infty|u_{lm}(r)|^2\,dr=\|\psi\|_{L^2}^2;$$

(b) $U$ is unitary, and for every $(u_{lm})\in K$ the finite-subset sums $\sum_{l\le N,\,|m|\le l}u_{lm}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ converge in $L^2$ to a function $\psi$ with $U\psi=(u_{lm})$;

(c) on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ every $f\in C^2$ satisfies, in the notation $\partial_r f$, $\Delta_{S^2}f$ of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]],
$$\Delta f=\partial_r^2f+\frac2r\partial_rf+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{S^2}f;$$

(d) for every $l\ge0$, $m$, and $u\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, the function $\psi:=u(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})\subseteq H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, its image under $U$ is the finite-support vector with $(l,m)$-entry $u$, and
$$-\Delta\psi=\frac1r\Bigl(-u''(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}u(r)\Bigr)Y_{lm}(\Omega),\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^3}|\nabla\psi|^2\,dx=\int_0^\infty\Bigl(\Bigl|u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr|^2+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}|u(r)|^2\Bigr)dr .$$

All statements are purely mathematical assertions about $L^2$ spaces, the
surface measure and the Laplacian; no physical interpretation and no statement
about operators with unbounded potentials is included.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real parameter $\hbar>0$. Let
$(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,-l\le m\le l}$ be the complete orthonormal family of $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ constructed in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and let
$H:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{lm}:-l\le m\le l,\ l\in\mathbb N\}$ be its algebraic (finite) span. Define operators
$A$ and $L_z$ on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ by the diagonal lemma
[[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]:

$$D(A):=\Bigl\{F:\sum_{l,m}l^2(l+1)^2\,|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad AF:=\sum_{l,m}l(l+1)\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},$$
$$D(L_z):=\Bigl\{F:\sum_{l,m}m^2\,|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad L_zF:=\sum_{l,m}\hbar m\,\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},$$

the sums being in the Hilbert-space norm ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Finally, for $F$ in the finite span
$H$ and a chart point $(\theta,\varphi)\in(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)$ write $F(\theta,\varphi)$ for the value of $F$
at $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)$ and put

$$(\mathcal S F)(\theta,\varphi):=-\frac1{\sin\theta}\partial_\theta\bigl(\sin\theta\,\partial_\theta F\bigr)(\theta,\varphi) -\frac1{\sin^2\theta}\partial_\varphi^2F(\theta,\varphi),\qquad (\mathcal D F)(\theta,\varphi):=-i\hbar\,\partial_\varphi F(\theta,\varphi),$$

where the partial derivatives are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then:

(a) $A$ and $L_z$ are self-adjoint operators on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ with the displayed domains; on $Y_{lm}$ they
act by $AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$ and $L_zY_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]); $A$ is nonnegative, $\langle AF,F\rangle\ge0$, and
$A\mathbf 1=0$;

(b) $H$ is a core of $A$ and of $L_z$: the finite truncations
$F_N:=\sum_{l\le N}\sum_{m}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm}$ of an element $F$ of $D(A)$ satisfy $F_N\to F$ and
$AF_N\to AF$ in $L^2$, and analogously with $L_z$;

(c) for every $F\in H$ and every chart point with $\sin\theta\ne0$,
$$\mathcal S F(\theta,\varphi)=(AF)(\theta,\varphi),\qquad \mathcal D F(\theta,\varphi)=(L_zF)(\theta,\varphi);$$

(d) for every $l$ the orthogonal projection $P_l$ of $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ onto the $(2l+1)$-dimensional span of
$Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}$ reduces both $A$ and $L_z$ ([[def-orthogonal-projection]]), i.e. $P_lA\subseteq AP_l$
and $P_lL_z\subseteq L_zP_l$; consequently $A$ and $L_z$ commute on the finite span $H$, and for every $F\in D(A)$ with
$\sum_{l,m}\bigl(l(l+1)\hbar m\bigr)^2|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2<\infty$ one has
$AL_zF=L_zAF=\sum_{l,m}l(l+1)\hbar m\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm}$. Writing $c_{lm}=\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle$ and $\lambda_l=l(l+1)$, the maximal product domains are $D(AL_z)=\{F\in L^2:\sum_{l,m}(\lambda_l\hbar m)^2|c_{lm}|^2<\infty\}$ and $D(L_zA)=D(A)\cap D(AL_z)$. Thus this is exactly the common domain $D(AL_z)\cap D(L_zA)=D(L_zA)$, while the two maximal product domains need not coincide. The product-weight condition alone does not imply $F\in D(A)$: the vector with coefficients $c_{l0}=1/l$ for $l\ge1$ and all other coefficients zero belongs to $L^2$, has zero product weight, but does not belong to $D(A)$. The product-weight condition is not automatic for all $F\in D(A)\cap D(L_z)$.

The differential expression $\mathcal S$ is evaluated only away from the poles, where the coordinate formulas are
defined; no claim is made about a maximal differential operator on all of $S^2$.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]) and let $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l}$ be the
functions of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] ([[def-complex-exponential]]).
Then $(Y_{lm})$ is a complete orthonormal family of the complex Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]):
the family is orthonormal, and if $F\in L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ satisfies
$\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma=0$ for all $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, then $F=0$ almost everywhere.
Consequently every $F$ has the expansion
$$F=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},\qquad \|F\|^2=\sum_{l,m}|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2,$$
with $\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle=\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma$ and finite-subset-net convergence
([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]).

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $M$ be a closed linear subspace of a real or complex Hilbert space $H$. Then every $x\in H$ has a unique decomposition

$$x=m+n,\qquad m\in M,\quad n\in M^\perp ,$$

so that $H=M\oplus M^\perp$ as a direct sum of the subspace $M$ and its orthogonal complement.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let $f$ be a bounded linear functional on $H$ ([[def-dual-space-of-a-normed-space]]). Then there is a unique $y\in H$ with

$$f(x)=\langle x,y\rangle\qquad\text{for every }x\in H,$$

and $\|f\|=\|y\|$, where $\|f\|$ is the dual norm ([[def-operator-norm]]). Under the first-variable-linear convention the representing vector depends conjugate-linearly and isometrically on $f$: if $f_i$ is represented by $y_i$ and $a,b$ are scalars, then $af_1+bf_2$ is represented by $\overline a\,y_1+\overline b\,y_2$.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$. Then every nonreal number belongs to
$\rho(T)$: $\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R\subseteq\rho(T)$. More precisely, for
$z=a+ib$ with $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $b\ne0$, and every $x\in D(T)$,
$$\|(T-z)x\|^2=\|(T-a)x\|^2+b^2\|x\|^2 ,$$
and consequently $\|R_T(z)\|\le 1/|\operatorname{Im}z|$. In particular
$\sigma(T)\subseteq\mathbb R$.
